subject: Data residency & PII handling — post-call clarifications and next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Julian Hayes <julian.hayes@acme-health.com>
Cc: acme-security@acme-health.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency & PII handling — post-call clarifications and next steps

Hi Julian / ACME security team,

Great to meet earlier — thank you for the detailed discovery call. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope an accurate proposal: 

Recap (from call)
- Primary objective: host patient PII and transaction records for EU-based patients within EU jurisdictions only.
- Retention ask: 7 years for logs/records (regulated financial/health use case).
- Auditability: exportable audit logs, tamper-evident, and KMS-backed encryption.
- DR/Failover: want to understand acceptable cross-region failover behavior and where backups can reside.

Open clarifying questions
1) For production PII: is the requirement strict "no copies outside EU at any time" (including backups and cross-region replicas), or is cross-region allowed for DR but only after documented approval/contractual controls?
2) For non-PII telemetry/logs: can they be routed to a separate region (US) for analytics, or must all telemetry stay in-region as well?
3) Desired RTO/RPO for failover? Is planned automated failover acceptable if we can guarantee encryption + notification, or do you require manual intervention?
4) Any preferred KMS provider / customer-managed key requirement (e.g., Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, HSM)?

What we can offer (high level)
- Region pinning: Redwood supports routing & storage pinning to region (EU) for primary model inference + KV/prefix caches.
- Backups: we can store encrypted backups in-region; cross-region backups are configurable but by default will not be enabled without customer approval.
- Failover: automated failover is supported with pre-authorized fallback plans; for strict residency we can implement a manual-failover runbook to avoid any cross-border replication without explicit approval.
- Audit & logs: configurable exportable audit logs; we can provide retention controls and signed log digests for tamper evidence.

Next steps I'd propose:
- Please confirm answers to the clarifying questions above.
- Send the ACME security questionnaire (if you haven’t already) so our security team can map controls directly.
- If those look good, let's schedule a technical deep dive (30–45m) w/ our infra/security leads to walk the architecture and DR options.

I’ve attached a short data-handling whitepaper + template DPA for your legal team to review.

Attachments: data_handling_whitepaper_v2.pdf (pdf), redwood_dpa_template.docx (docx)

Thanks,

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0138

From: Julian Hayes <julian.hayes@acme-health.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data residency & PII handling — post-call clarifications and next steps

Vivek — thanks for the summary and for the attachments. A few notes from ACME security/legal: 

High-level requirements
- PII residency: Production patient PII must remain within EU physical jurisdictions at all times. That includes primary data stores, backups, and any asynchronous replicas. Cross-border movement is permitted only under a documented and contractual exception (e.g., signed addendum).
- Backups: Backups must be encrypted with a customer-approved KMS, and by default kept in the same region. Cross-region backup location requires explicit approval.
- Failover: For DR testing we can allow cross-region replication to a pre-approved DR region, but automated failover to that region must be configurable and require a pre-authorized policy.
- Logs & telemetry: Audit logs that contain PII must be stored in-region. Aggregated, de-identified telemetry can be exported for analytics but must be documented.
- Retention: Logs and records — 7 years. Must support tamper-evident retention and certified deletion on request within contractual SLA.

We’re attaching the ACME security questionnaire for your team to complete: acme_security_questionnaire.xlsx

Also please add a copy of your most recent SOC 2 and a data flow diagram so we can run this through our compliance review.

For scheduling: we prefer a technical call on Thursday morning CET if possible. I'll loop legal if we move to contractual exceptions.

Thanks,

Julian Hayes
Head of Security Operations | ACME Health
julian.hayes@acme-health.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Julian Hayes <julian.hayes@acme-health.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency & PII handling — post-call clarifications and next steps

Thanks Julian — very clear and appreciated. Looping in Monica (Customer Solutions) and Aditya (Security/Compliance) to map ACME requirements to our controls.

Answering your clarifying questions inline (quoted where helpful):

> 1) Strict "no copies outside EU at any time"?
We can support a strict in-region-only posture for production PII. That includes primary stores, backups, and KV/cache persistence if requested. For hosted customers we have an EU-only tenancy option; for the strictest posture we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with committed EU-only capacity.

> 2) Non-PII telemetry routing?
Aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry can be routed to a separate analytics region by default. If you require all telemetry to remain in-region we can enforce that via route policies.

> 3) RTO/RPO and automated failover?
Automated failover is supported, but for customers requiring strict residency we offer a manual-failover configuration and pre-authorized DR runbook so there is no automatic cross-border replication without customer consent. If you are open to DR replication to a pre-approved DR region, we can document it in the DPA/addendum.

> 4) Preferred KMS?
We support customer-managed keys (CMK) with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS. We also support HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments. Please specify which provider you prefer and whether ACME will provide key material or require Redwood-managed keys under a specific policy.

Attached for ACME review: redwood_soc2_report_2025.pdf (SOC 2 Type II), data_handling_whitepaper_v2.pdf (controls summary), redwood_dpa_template.docx

Proposed next steps:
- Monica / Aditya to complete ACME questionnaire and provide a data flow diagram.
- Schedule a 45m technical session (security + infra) — Monica, Aditya, and I will join.
- Post-call: we’ll produce a short scoping doc outlining configuration options (hosted EU tenancy vs Dedicated vs Private) and recommended contractual language for residency & backups.

Let us know preferred time slots for Thursday morning CET or Friday CET.

Regards,

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_soc2_report_2025.pdf (pdf), data_handling_whitepaper_v2.pdf (pdf), redwood_dpa_template.docx (docx)
